  delivers, forms a parabola. Real main cables sit between the two, close to the parabola. Having no bending stiffness, the cable settles into the one shape in which every part is in
  pure tension, gathering the pull of the hangers into a large force running along the cable toward each end.
  Where the cable meets a tower, that force has a vertical and a horizontal component. The towers take the vertical part. The cables pass over saddles at the tower tops, delivering the
  downward force into the towers as compression, which travels to foundations on bedrock or deep caissons. Because the cable pulls roughly equally on both sides of each saddle, the
  horizontal forces largely cancel, leaving the tower loaded mostly along its axis.
  The horizontal component ends at the anchorages. At each end the main cables splay into strands tied into massive concrete blocks or rock tunnels, which resist the pull through sheer
  weight, friction, and the passive resistance of the ground behind them. On a major bridge those forces run to tens of thousands of tonnes, which is why anchorages are often the
  bulkiest structures on the site. Self-anchored designs, a rarer variant, tie the cables into the deck instead, which then carries the horizontal force as compression.
  Dead load is steady; live load and wind are not. A single heavy truck would tend to pull a flexible cable into a local kink, so a stiffening girder or truss in the deck spreads
  concentrated loads across many hangers. Aerodynamics matters just as much. The 1940 collapse of the Tacoma Narrows Bridge showed that a slender deck can twist in wind until it tears
  itself apart; modern decks use streamlined box sections or open trusses that let air pass without feeding those oscillations.
  The result is a clean division of labour: hangers and cables in tension, towers in compression, anchorages holding against the ground, and the deck distributing load and resisting
  wind. By asking each element to do only what it does best, the suspension bridge reaches spans no other bridge form can match.
✻ Baked for 44s · done 8:35 PM
